title: Check the formula before you trust it
goal: Catch a formula that's mis-ranged or fragile before it quietly corrupts your whole tracker.

blocks.title: A wrong total looks exactly like a right one
blocks.body:
Here's what makes sheet errors dangerous: a wrong number looks just as tidy as a right one. There's no red squiggle, no warning — just a total that's quietly off.

So you never trust a formula on faith. You test it on one row where you already know the answer. If AI's formula agrees with your hand-calculation on that row, it'll hold for the rest. Two things trip formulas most: the wrong range, and a blank cell.

blocks.question: Your marks sit in B2:B42 (41 students). The AI hands you =AVERAGE(B2:B41) for the class average. What do you do?

options.text: Paste it — it's an AVERAGE formula, that's what you asked for
Catch it — the range stops at B41 and silently drops your last student; fix it to B2:B42
Assume the AI counted the rows correctly

blocks.explanation: Caught it. 👏 The formula runs fine and shows a clean number — but it's averaging 40 students, not 41. An off-by-one range is the classic silent slip. Checking the range is the skill no tool replaces.

blocks.question: For attendance %, the AI gives =C2/D2. One new student has a blank in D (total classes not entered yet). What happens?

options.text: It shows #DIV/0! — dividing by an empty cell breaks; wrap it, e.g. =IFERROR(C2/D2, ""), so blanks don't crash the column
The sheet fills in the missing number on its own

blocks.explanation: Right — an empty cell reads as zero, and dividing by zero throws #DIV/0!, which can cascade down your whole tracker. A robust formula handles the blanks you'll inevitably have. That's thinking one step ahead of the sheet.

blocks.question: How ready do you feel to sanity-check an AI formula on a known row before relying on it?
